title: spatial-ui-polish — SDK source map (code-level dependency contract)
authority: Read directly from the locally resolved PICO Spatial SDK 6.1.9 sources jars in the Gradle module cache. Line spans are the exact spans in those archives. This map is the contract later tasks cite instead of guessing overloads. Nothing here is native-tested until the checkpoint says so.

bomPom.note: Every member resolves to 6.1.9. The BOM was already present in the local cache before this work; nothing was provisioned for this map.

declarations.signature: @Stable fun Modifier.backgroundMaterial(enable: Boolean = true, style: Material = Material.Regular): Modifier
declarations.notes: View-level material rendered by the OS compositor; applied only when enable && (SpatialBuild.isSpatialPlatform() || core BuildConfig.DEBUG). It is a LayoutModifierNode that consumes 1px of depth (DEPTH=-1, BACK_OFFSET=1) and sets SpatialGraphicsLayerScope.backgroundMaterial = Material.toFrameworkViewMaterial(): None 0, Regular 1, Thick 2, Thickest 3, Thin 4. Exposes enable/style only — no blur radius, refraction, lensing or backdrop sampling parameters.

declarations.signature: enum class Material { None, Regular, Thick, Thickest, Thin }
declarations.notes: KDoc: Regular = base layer (Window, Augment, TabBar, ToolBar); Thick = large elevated layer (Dialog, Sheet, Menu); Thickest = small elevated layer (Tooltip, Text selector); Thin = small elevated elements (Box, Button, CheckBox) and 'Currently, It has no effect for the Window'. toFrameworkWindowBackgroundInt maps Thin -> 0, identical to None: Thin is not a window material.

declarations.signature: public val WindowContainer.enableMaterialBackground: Boolean get() = properties.enableMaterialBackground ?: true; WindowContainerProperties.enableMaterialBackground: Boolean? = null; manager merge: dsl.enableMaterialBackground ?: default.enableMaterialBackground; default from ContainerMaterialBackground.fromBundle(meta-data `pico.spatial.windowcontainer.materialbackground`, default REGULAR=1)
declarations.notes: A null DSL value means INHERIT: the manager fills it from the target Activity's manifest meta-data (0 = NONE, anything else = REGULAR), and the manifest default is REGULAR. So the effective default is glass ON unless the manifest says "0" or the DSL says false. Platform side agrees: SUIWindowContainer.kt:82-84 provides LocalIsMaterialBackgroundEnabled = isSupportWindowMaterial && (enableMaterialBackground ?: true); SpatialActivityDelegateImpl.kt:169-176 applies Material.Regular to the Activity window when the merged value == true. The simplified docs' `true (default)` is therefore correct as an effective default, not as the declared type.

declarations.id: Motion duration scale is pinned by the SDK
declarations.signature: internal fun enableMotion() { WindowRecomposerPolicy.setFactory { rootView -> rootView.createLifecycleAwareWindowRecomposer(EmptyCoroutineContext + FixedMotionDurationScale) } }; FixedMotionDurationScale.scaleFactor = 1f
declarations.notes: Installed from a ContentProvider at process start. Consequence: Compose animations in a SpatialUI app ignore the system animator duration scale, so an OS-level 'remove animations' preference does NOT shorten them. Reduced motion therefore has to be an app-owned option (optionally seeded from Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE as an advisory signal).

rulings.question: Is Material.Thin a window-glass solution?
rulings.ruling: No. As a WINDOW material it maps to 0 (None) and its KDoc says it has no effect for the Window (platform/Material.kt:34-38, 47). As a VIEW material (Modifier.backgroundMaterial) it maps to 4 and is documented for small elevated elements such as Box/Button/CheckBox. The kit uses the system Regular glass for window roots and reserves Thin for inner elements only. The vendor window-background.md example that reapplies Thin on a window root after switching the system glass off is not carried into this skill.

rulings.question: What does WindowContainer(enableMaterialBackground = null) mean?
rulings.ruling: Inherit. Core merges a null DSL value with the target Activity's manifest meta-data `pico.spatial.windowcontainer.materialbackground` (default REGULAR = on). The composition local and the Activity window both treat the merged value as on unless it is explicitly off. Writing `enableMaterialBackground = true` blindly is unnecessary but harmless; leaving it null is the documented default. To go opaque or custom, set the DSL value to false (non-default containers) or the manifest to "0" (the launcher DefaultWindowContainer), then own the root background explicitly.

rulings.question: Does PicoTheme provide a text foreground for ordinary layout surfaces?
rulings.ruling: No. PicoTheme provides colour scheme, typography, indication and tokens but not LocalContentColor, whose default is Color.Unspecified; Text and Icon fall through to it. Only built-ins provide content colour internally. The kit's theme wrapper provides LocalContentColor = labelPrimary on the theme root, and every polished surface re-provides the foreground that matches its own background (labelPrimary on glass/neutral fills, labelPrimaryLight on accent/dark fills).

rulings.question: Which components already own hover, so wrappers must not add spatialHoverEffect?
rulings.ruling: Button, IconButton (via BasicButton), ToggleButton, ButtonChip/ToggleableChip/RemovableChip, CheckBox, Switch, Slider family, TextField/TextArea, SegmentItem, ListItem, Option, PageControl, ScrollIndicator, DatePicker/TimePicker/NumberField, MenuItem and TabBar apply spatialHoverEffect internally. Wrappers pass hover-neutral modifiers to them. Custom surfaces that are NOT built-ins (PolishSurface in enhanced mode) may apply spatialHoverEffect exactly once, before clickable.

rulings.question: How is 'one configurable accent' expressed in 6.1.9?
rulings.ruling: Through ColorScheme.interaction (fixed semantic role; default SubBlue100 #3377FF in DisplayP3), overridden via systemColorScheme(context).copy(interaction = ...). There is no accent/onAccent role; foreground on accent fills is labelPrimaryLight.

rulings.question: Can reduced motion come from a platform preference?
rulings.ruling: Not automatically: the SDK pins the Compose motion duration scale to 1. The kit owns a reduceMotion option (persisted app setting) and may seed it from Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0 as an advisory default; reduced transparency and increased contrast are app-owned options (no SpatialUI preference exists in 6.1.9 sources).

rulings.question: Can the window corner radius be tuned?
rulings.ruling: No. The 6.0 vault FAQ states the window corner radius is a fixed system value (32 dp visual) with no DSL or manifest entry; only the glass panel can be disabled. Inner surfaces therefore harmonise with a 32 dp window: cards 16-24 dp, buttons per ButtonDefaults.

declaredNativeUntestedHere: system Material.Regular window glass (DefaultWindowContainer / WindowContainer / Augment / Subwindow / Toolbar)
Material.Thick dialogs, sheets, popups, menus; Material.Thickest snackbar/tooltips
